Emergency situation?

Do not waste time reading if the animal is not breathing or unconscious. Call a vet immediately.

Emergency

Step-by-step actions when every minute counts, and the signs that mean a vet visit today.

Critical situations

Found an Animal on the Street CRITICALFound a Kitten on the Street CRITICALCan't Urinate or Defecate CRITICALDifficulty Breathing CRITICALPoisoning CRITICALForeign Object CRITICALSeizures CRITICALSevere Bleeding CRITICALInjury or Fall CRITICALInjured by a Child: First Aid and Prevention CRITICALVomiting or Diarrhea (with Blood) CRITICALRefusing Food and Water CRITICALTemperature Issues / Hypothermia CRITICALLoss of Consciousness / Weakness CRITICALHind Leg Paralysis CRITICALHeatstroke CRITICALSevere Allergic Reaction CRITICALBurns CRITICAL

See a vet TODAY (do not wait)

  • Cat hasn't eaten for >24h, kitten >12h.
  • Blood in urine or stool.
  • Frequent vomiting (3+ times a day).
  • Prolonged diarrhea.
  • Eye won't open or has discharge.
  • Severe limping.
  • Urination problems.
Not a substitute for a vet

The information in this app comes from open sources and the experience of cat owners. It does not replace a consultation or an examination by a vet. Decisions about your pet's health and care are the owner's to make — if in any doubt, contact a vet.
